column1: # THE NEW ENGINE'S OWN ORACLE -- read ONLY by zig/src/authproxy/route_vectors_test.zig.
# Unlike path_vectors.tsv (the SHARED oracle read by three suites), this file
# has exactly one consumer: the Zig auth proxy's route engine. That single-
# consumer design is the concrete form of the spec's claim that the dual-matcher
# obligation for git rules ENDS -- so this file must NOT be staged into the
# addon-tests derivation, and no Python matcher reads it.
# TAB-separated. Blank lines and `#` comments ignored. Four kinds:
#       splitTarget (strip fragment, split at first `?`) then canonicalize:
#       split the PATH on `/` FIRST, percent-decode each segment ONCE. Each
#       expected segment is its own TAB field -- which is how `grp%2Fproj`
#       stays ONE segment whose value CONTAINS a slash. A row with zero
#       expected segments means the empty path (`/`).
#       The canonicalizer refuses it outright; the core denies (403, no
#       classify then authorize under the named grant fixture (defined in the
#       test file). A route that classify denies is a deny here too.
# ================= canon: the INVERTED oracle vs path_vectors.tsv:62-64 =========
# The legacy normalizer INFLATES `grp%2Fproj` into extra segments; this engine
# must produce the OPPOSITE structural claim -- one segment whose value holds a
# slash. That inversion is the entire point of segment-first single-decode.
